column3: “A day is coming of the LORD” is rendered “a day is coming for the LORD”; NASB supplies “taken from you.”
“For the battle” is rendered “to battle,” and “lain with” “ravished.”
“Like the day he fought” is rendered “as when He fights.”
“On the face of Jerusalem” is rendered “in front of Jerusalem,” and “depart” “move”; NASB supplies “by.”
“Azal” is spelled “Azel,” and “with you” “with Him”; NASB adds “yes.”
“Splendid ones and frost” is rendered “the luminaries will dwindle,” following a different reading. The meaning is uncertain.
“One day” is rendered “a unique day”; NASB adds “For” and “but.”
“Go out” is rendered “flow out”; NASB adds “as well as.”
“The LORD will be one and his name one” is rendered “the LORD will be the only one, and His name the only one.”
“Change … like the Arabah” is rendered “changed into a plain”; NASB supplies “Jerusalem,” and capitalizes the gate names.
“Total destruction” is rendered “curse,” and “remain” “dwell”; NASB adds “for.”
NASB supplies “while” and renders “its” as “their.”
“A panic of the LORD” is rendered “a panic from the LORD”; NASB supplies “will fall on them.”
“At Jerusalem” follows the Hebrew; the meaning may be “against Jerusalem.”
“Livestock” is rendered “cattle”; NASB moves “like this plague” to the front.
“As often as a year in a year” is rendered “from year to year,” “bow down” “worship,” and “the festival of Tabernacles” “the Feast of Booths.”
“Bow down” is rendered “worship,” and “clans” “families.”
“Not on them” is rendered “then no rain will fall on them,” supplying “rain”; the Hebrew is elliptical.
“Punishment for sin” is rendered “punishment.”
NASB supplies “inscribed”; “pots” is rendered “cooking pots.”
“Pot” is rendered “cooking pot.”
